moat_against: Commodity cycle rules demand - customers cut capex fast when oil falls, and HAL printed net losses in 2016, 2019 and 2020
Pricing power erodes in oversupplied North American pressure pumping; E&P consolidation strengthens customer bargaining power
SLB and Baker Hughes contest the same programs with comparable technology - no program is uncontested
Work is re-won project by project - no long-term lock-in beyond current integrated contracts
Long-term energy-transition / oil-demand risk caps the terminal story
moat_for: Big-3 oligopoly scale - #2 global oilfield servicer, leader in North American completions and pressure pumping
Proprietary technology: LOGIX autonomous drilling, Zeus electric fracturing, Landmark / DecisionSpace digital platform
Integrated well delivery across drilling, evaluation, completion and production creates switching friction once embedded
Global footprint diversifies North America shale exposure with longer-cycle international and offshore work
Through-cycle cash generation: owner's earnings positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years, with buybacks shrinking the count 2.1%/yr
moat_justification: Big-3 oligopoly scale as the #2 global oilfield servicer and North American completions leader, proprietary drilling/fracturing/digital technology and integrated well delivery that creates real switching friction, plus a global footprint that diversifies shale exposure - but demand is set by the commodity cycle (net losses in 2016, 2019, 2020), pricing power erodes when pressure pumping is oversupplied, consolidated E&P customers bargain hard, work is re-won project by project, and SLB/Baker Hughes contest every program; moderate moat, CAP 8.5y.
name: Halliburton Company
one_liner: Cyclical Big-3 oilfield servicer, moat 5/10 - at $32.85 on TTM owner's earnings of $1.80/share (OE yield 5.49%) it does not clear 15%: weighted IRR 8.45%, weighted IV@15% $15.47; it clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$15.47, and even the super-bull case only returns 13.88%.

sbc_override.reason: DATA_GAP:sbc - SBC missing for fiscal years 2023, 2024, 2025 of the last 3 under the engine's tags. The filer's own reported FY2025 stock-based compensation cost from its 10-K Note 14 fills the gap; the engine applies this single value to every missing period. The true per-year series in the same table is $219M (FY2023) / $223M (FY2024) / $213M (FY2025), so applying $213M to all three years is within $10M of the true figure in each year and is immaterial to the median base (under $0.02/share in the median year).
sbc_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-06, accession 0000045012-26-000015), Note 14 Stock-based Compensation table: stock-based compensation cost $213 million for 2025, $223 million for 2024 and $219 million for 2023. EDGAR companyfacts carries ShareBasedCompensation only through 2014, so the engine found no FY SBC for 2023-2025.
